石くびり.name: Ishikubiri
石くびり.desc: On the Soba Kaido (soba road), with a nostalgic look like a Showa-era diner. A popular shop with celebrity autographs covering an entire wall. Its chewy noodles and chewy fish cake, among the best of any Okinawa soba shop, shine. Its taro (ta-imo) dishes are certified as "100-Year Food" by the Agency for Cultural Affairs.

I went to eat here in September 2024😄

On my Okinawa soba rounds, I visited "Ishikubiri" in Aza Higashi, Motobu Town. Using an afternoon of hourly leave, I came to this shop with an atmosphere just like a Showa-era diner. Even the exterior is well-worn, with a somehow nostalgic feel. It's a shop you can tell at a glance is loved by locals😊

When you step inside, celebrity autographs and newspaper articles covering an entire wall jump out at you, and you can tell it's a popular shop rooted in the community. There's also tatami seating, and it's a relaxed space as if you were at home✨

Menu

The menu has not only "Ishikubiri soba" but also "vegetable soba," "beef and bean sprout soba," and even "eel," so there's plenty of variety. But here, of course, I tried ordering the "Ishikubiri soba" bearing the shop's name. The price is a reasonable ¥800 too, and my excitement grew while I waited.
Ishikubiri soba ¥800

And out came the "Ishikubiri soba"🍜. First, when I took a sip of the broth, the pork bone comes through firmly, and the saltiness felt strong too. However, since it's a bit on the salty side, people watching their salt might find it a little heavy.
Ishikubiri soba ¥800

The noodles are medium-thick with a chewy texture, and they have such springiness that it makes you think, maybe they're house-made? These noodles that grab the broth well are very satisfying and very delicious👍 What especially moved me was the "fish cake (kamaboko)" topping! This fish cake has without a doubt the No.1 chewiness of all the Okinawa soba shops I've eaten at, and it surprised me into thinking, "Was kamaboko always this delicious?" Fish cake, which I don't usually pay much attention to, has a star-level presence here🌟

The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) and bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki) are also well seasoned through, and the umami of the meat spreads out. However, some slightly sinewy parts remain, so people looking for tenderness might mind that.

Rating (9/15): Just plain tasty😄 I thought the noodles and fish cake in particular were high-level. I thought the deliciousness of the fish cake is hard to find elsewhere, so why not give it a try once? As expected of a shop on the Okinawa Soba Kaido😄

What I ordered from the menu this time was, of course, the famous "Choju single-noodle soba" (¥1,200)! The newspaper article said something like 4.5 meters, but looking at it in person, maybe it's not quite that long? But it's definitely not the length of a normal noodle~😅 This single noodle has a flat shape like kishimen, and it's amazing that it really is made as one strand!
Choju single-noodle soba ¥1,200
Choju single-noodle soba ¥1,200

When you lift it with your chopsticks, the way it just keeps going and going is hugely impactful. However, unlike regular Okinawa soba, honestly this flat shape makes it hard to slurp😆 The noodle texture is chewy.

The broth seems to be a combined broth with plenty of pork bone. The umami of the pork bone comes out well, and it's finished with richness🍲 The toppings are three kinds: pig's feet (tebichi), bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku). The tebichi is simmered until meltingly tender, full of collagen and delicious! The hon-soki has a sweetish seasoning and a bit of sinewy texture, but it's satisfying in its own way. The braised pork belly is also finished meltingly tender, with a nice balance of fat and lean. On the side there's fish cake, and interestingly, a condiment like chili oil crisp. Adding this partway through changes the taste of the broth so you can enjoy it two ways, which I think is a good idea🌶️
Condiments

The location is Sakimotobu, Motobu Town, near the Shiokawa bus stop on National Route 449. Since it's a mobile food vendor, the hours and location may change, so it might be better to check in advance. There's parking for a few cars in front of the shop, but it's along the road, so be careful. The eating area is open-air, covered by a green tent, with colorful picnic tables lined up, so you can enjoy your meal in a resort mood. It looks especially pleasant on sunny days☀️

The menu is wide-ranging too, from the standard Okinawa soba to soki soba, yushi-dofu soba, and more, reasonably priced at ¥800 for medium and ¥950 for large. There are set menus too; the jushi set is ¥1,000 medium and ¥1,150 large. There's also an unusual "ASIA yakisoba" for ¥1,000, which piqued my curiosity🍝 The drink menu is extensive too, so you can enjoy very Okinawan drinks like Okinawa green juice smoothies and mango smoothies. Acerola soda and shikuwasa soda are Motobu Town recommendations as well, and it's nice to be able to enjoy local flavors🥤

Rating (9/15): The single noodle at "Okinawa Choju Soba" definitely makes for an impactful experience! The taste was plainly tasty too, and it was a warm shop where you can feel love for the local area. I think the unusual single-noodle style is worth experiencing at least once😊 It's a slightly different way of eating from regular Okinawa soba, but that was all part of a fun experience. When you're heading toward Motobu, please do stop by!🌺

Chinen soba is satisfying, characterized by chewy springiness and wavy noodles that snap off with a pop, while Nago soba is a firm straight noodle widely used in northern Okinawa, with reliable deliciousness. I was curious about both, but this time I followed the staff's recommendation and chose Chinen Seimenjo's "wavy noodles."

Besides an orthodox lineup of soki soba, braised pork belly soba, pig's feet (tebichi) soba, soft-bone pork rib soba, and so on, I was also curious about an unusual one, the "vegetable soba" limited to 5 servings a day😁 The vegetable soba is a Maruyoshi-style dish topped with garlic-flavored stir-fried garlic chives, carrots, bean sprouts, cabbage, and pork, so I'd like to try it next time. Looking at the Maruyoshi soba that was brought out after a while, it was a visibly hearty bowl, packed with toppings starting with the soft-bone pork ribs😋

First, the customary gulp of broth. It's bonito-broth-based, and I got the impression it's finished quite rich compared to other shops😊 But rather than a standout personality, my impression was of plainly tasty bonito broth.
Maruyoshi soba, medium (Chinen Seimenjo's wavy noodles) ¥900

Next, I try the wavy noodles I chose. Eating them, they were finished on the soft side overall. They had the popping texture typical of wavy noodles, but personally I felt they could have had a bit more springiness🍜

When I picked up the soft-bone pork ribs topping with my chopsticks, the cartilage part had a really crunchy texture, a type you rarely get at other shops😲 While many shops simmer their soft-bone ribs until meltingly tender, Maruyoshi's cartilage keeps a firm texture, and I thought it's rare for it to be this crunchy. It may divide opinions. On the other hand, the meat part has a bit of sinewy texture.

Rating (9/15): Overall, honestly, I'd say it's average~. It's a soba shop rooted in the community here in the Kanna area of Ginoza Village✨ It also has a bit of personality, with the fun of choosing your noodles and the crunchy soft-bone pork ribs, so why not stop by when you're on a drive up north?😊

This time I visited "Okinawa Soba SOBA DAY" in Daido, Naha. I ate here in October 2024😁 The shop's exterior is simple, and the mostly white sign catches the eye✨.
Okinawa Soba SOBA DAY
Okinawa Soba SOBA DAY

When you enter the shop, the ticket machine jumps out at you🎟. It seems to be a meal ticket system here, and the menu is extensive. What I chose this time was the "double-meat soba"! A luxurious bowl where you can enjoy both braised pork belly and chashu. When I bought my ticket and took a seat, the counter seats were full and it was bustling. It really is a popular shop😊.
Meal ticket machine set up near the entrance
This shop's name is "Okinawa Soba SOBA DAY," and indeed "Okinawa Soba Day" is October 17😄

Since I came to eat around Okinawa Soba Day, there was also a campaign pork dish called "Pineapple Pork." This time I went with the regular "double-meat soba," but it seems the usual broth had been upgraded to one made with "Pineapple Pork," so I was looking forward to it😆
Apparently every broth has been upgraded to "Pineapple Pork"😄
Double-meat soba ¥970

The "double-meat soba" was brought out after a wait of a few minutes. It's a very beautiful-looking bowl, with colorful toppings. Chashu, braised pork belly, and... fu (wheat gluten)? were on top. The fu was a little unexpected, with a distinctive fluffy texture. It has almost no taste of its own.
They said the broth uses Pineapple Pork, but the bonito broth really comes through in it🍜.
Double-meat soba ¥970
The noodles are medium-thin and straight, with a slightly firm texture. The overall balance is good, but if you ask whether there's any distinctive feature worth noting, it feels ordinary.

And as for the meat, both the braised pork belly and chashu are the type where a bit of sinewy texture remains. This may divide likes and dislikes😅. They're simmered thoroughly, but in terms of tenderness I'd say they're one step short.

The shop's atmosphere is casual, and it seemed bustling with local customers. It's a compact setup with only counter seats, and it's a nice point that it's easy to visit casually even on your own. Also, island chili peppers and vinegar are provided as condiments, so you can customize it to your liking, which is nice🌶️.
There's vinegar among the condiments too.

By the way, when I googled "SOBA DAY," it seems to be run by someone who previously trained at "EIBUN," which I introduce in "Recommended Okinawa soba shops I'd like you to try at least once." That raised my expectations, but my impression of the actual taste was just plain tasty. Of course, it's a reliable bowl.

Rating (9/15): Overall, it was plainly tasty Okinawa soba. I wanted one more surprise. It might be good to stop by once when visiting as a tourist, but whether you'd come back may depend on your taste? Next time I'd like to try a different dish🍴!

夢ノ弥.name: Yume no Ya
夢ノ弥.desc: Okinawa soba, limited to 30 servings a day, made by a shop specializing in rich chicken, pork bone, and seafood tsukemen. The clean pork bone broth with no off-odor and the meltingly tender braised pork belly are delicious; just one step short of recommended level. Cashless payment is a plus too.
t: I ate here in April 2024😄 Every time I drove along National Route 330 there was a conspicuous sign, so I'd been curious for a long time, and I finally went😆
The sign for "Yume no Ya" along National Route 330
It's "Okinawa soba" made by a rich tsukemen specialty shop😁 Doesn't that alone sound delicious? lol And it's limited to 30 servings a day! My expectations are high.
"Yume no Ya" (rich chicken, pork bone, and seafood tsukemen. That alone sounds delicious😆)
A promotional poster for "Chicken, Pork Bone & Seafood Okinawa Soba" posted at the entrance
The meal ticket machine set up right inside the entrance (it accepts cashless, which is wonderful👍)

When you go inside, the meal ticket machine is right in front of you. It's a tsukemen specialty shop, but my only target was the "Okinawa soba," so I ordered the "Chicken, Pork Bone & Seafood Okinawa Soba." And it accepts cashless, which is wonderful👍 I paid with Rakuten Pay, which earns Rakuten points😆
Menu (besides Okinawa soba, there are all kinds of tsukemen that look delicious😆)
Soba description board
There was also a description of the soba. My expectations are high😄
Chicken, Pork Bone & Seafood Okinawa Soba ¥800
The Okinawa soba made by a tsukemen specialty shop arrived😁 First, the broth.
It's a broth with plenty of pork bone, with no off-odor and a clean feel. I thought it was different from other shops' pork bone broths. Delicious😄
Chicken, Pork Bone & Seafood Okinawa Soba ¥800

Next, the noodles. They're thin and straight. They feel soft and are just plain tasty. The braised pork belly topping is meltingly tender with no sinewy texture, and delicious; I wanted to eat a bit more😆

Rating (10/15): The broth is a pork-bone-based broth you won't find at other shops, and the braised pork belly topping was delicious too. Since it's Okinawa soba made by a tsukemen specialty shop, I feel I may have set the bar too high; it's delicious, but I thought it's just one step short of recommended level.

ゆし豆腐そば専門店 わらいそば.name: Yushi-dofu Soba Senmonten Warai Soba
ゆし豆腐そば専門店 わらいそば.desc: A two-faced shop: yushi-dofu soba specialist by day, izakaya (pub) by night. Fresh noodles from Terukina Noodle Factory, yushi-dofu from Unashi Tofu, and a ginger condiment that feels fresh. A memorable shop where I was able to use the ¥500 coupon earned by completing the stamp rally.
t: ― 2nd Visit (July 2024) ―
I came to eat here in July 2024 😄 Actually, the other day I completed the Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally and got a ¥500 coupon. Since I had it, I thought I’d use it, so I chose this place this time 😆
The ¥500 discount coupon from Warai Soba that I received for completing the Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally. I used it this time 😄
Yushi-dofu specialty shop Warai Soba
Yushi-dofu specialty shop Warai Soba

Menu

They also ship nationwide
Last time I had the yushi-dofu soba, but honestly I couldn’t really tell the taste of the broth (^_^;) So this time I went with a regular Okinawa soba.
Okinawa soba, large　¥750 (this time I used the ¥500 discount coupon, so I got it for ¥250 😁)
Here it comes! It looks like an ordinary Okinawa soba. What will it taste like?!

First the broth. Yeah, last time the yushi-dofu was mixed in and I couldn’t tell the broth’s flavor well, but this one has a pork-bone-forward taste. It seems to be a blended broth, but the pork-bone flavor comes through clearly.
Okinawa soba, large　¥750 (this time I used the ¥500 discount coupon, so I got it for ¥250 😁)

Honestly, the Okinawa soba at Warai Soba is just plain tasty. They’re not doing anything particularly unusual, but the flavor is stable. I thought it’s the kind of shop where local people come to eat on a daily basis.
I was glad I could use the stamp rally’s ¥500 coupon too 😁
Rating (9/15): It’s just plain tasty. When you’re stopping by near Nezashibu in Tomigusuku City, why not give it a try? 😄
― 1st Visit (January 2024) ―

I ate here in January 2024. This is my first Okinawa soba outing of the new year 😄 This shop is a participating shop in the “13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (2023.10.1–2024.2.29),” and I went as the 31st of 34 shops 😊
Yushi-dofu soba specialty shop Warai Soba
Entrance of Yushi-dofu soba specialty shop Warai Soba
Yushi-dofu soba specialty shop Warai Soba
The ticket machine installed near the entrance inside the shop

This time I planned to eat before going surfing, my hobby (Itoman City: Suicide Cliff Point), so I waited in the parking lot from about 15 minutes before the 11:00 opening 😄 At exactly 11:00 I walked in as the very first customer 😆
The menu I would order was the “yushi-dofu soba with braised pork belly topping” 👍 introduced in the stamp rally booklet.

There was a QR code for cashless payment (PayPay) at what looked like a checkout counter next to the ticket machine, so I told the staff “I’d like to pay with PayPay,” and the answer was “Sorry, we can’t use PayPay” (^0^;)
In the end I ordered the “yushi-dofu soba with braised pork belly topping” from the ticket machine with cash (^0^;) I wish every Okinawa soba shop would go cashless soon 😁
Menu: What I ordered was the No. 2 most popular one. I have high hopes 😆
Menu: It’s kind of them to explain the top 5 popularity ranking, lol
Explanation of the shop’s commitment to its Okinawa soba, and the menu
Gift and takeout menu
After ordering I looked at the menu for a while, but even though I was the first customer of the day, I thought it was taking a little while.
Okinawa soba, the soul food of Okinawans, is something I want to eat quickly (^0^;)
Inside the shop
The photo above shows the situation inside the shop, and I thought “this feels like an izakaya.”
Then, looking closely at the sign outside, it seems they are an Okinawa soba shop by day and an izakaya at night (^0^;) That explains the interior (^0^;)
Yushi-dofu soba with braised pork belly topping　¥800
I was killing time looking at the menu, thinking “it’s taking long,” and it finally came? (^0^;)

As usual I start with the broth 😄 The menu’s explanation said “a blend of stock from ‘bonito + pork bone,’ ‘chicken bones,’ ‘kelp,’ and ‘5 kinds of vegetables,’” but my impression when drinking it was that of yushi-dofu soup (^0^;) Honestly I couldn’t tell what it was based on. Sorry 🙏
But it has a gentle flavor and is just plain tasty.
Yushi-dofu soba with braised pork belly topping　¥800

Next, the noodles. These are Terukina Noodle Factory’s medium-thick wavy fresh noodles, I was told. They’re chewy as expected, but to me they didn’t seem to cling to the broth, and the broth and noodles felt separate.
There was a little ginger as a condiment, and mixing it into the broth gave a refreshing taste that felt new. Ginger with Okinawa soba broth may be surprisingly good 😄
The braised pork belly is melt-in-your-mouth tender and just plain tasty.

Rating (9/15): It’s just plain tasty. However, the broth tasted more like yushi-dofu soup than Okinawa soba broth, and it was hard to tell what the broth was based on. Also, the noodles are chewy and just plain tasty, but I couldn’t feel them mingling with the broth, and the broth and noodles felt separate. The ginger accent isn’t found at other shops, which I thought was nice, and the braised pork belly was melt-in-your-mouth tender and just plain tasty.

ニューロイヤル.name: New Royal
ニューロイヤル.desc: A stylish Okinawa soba shop in Kinaka, Uruma City, opened in December 2023. It used to be a mozuku seaweed shop, and comes with a “How to Eat Course” that makes it fun to change the flavor with original condiments such as umai-ume (plum) and shikuwasa vinegar. The signature is the Royal Soba, which also has yushi-dofu from the local Shirin-gawa Tofu.
t: I went to eat here in January 2024 😊 It was during the “13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (2023.10.1–2024.2.29)” and I was one shop away from clearing it. I wanted to eat at a participating shop, but there was no final-shop candidate in Uruma City, where I had business, so I ate at this shop that I happened to find online 😄
New Royal (It was lunchtime and the customers’ cars filled the lot, so I couldn’t photograph the noren properly, sorry (^0^;))
New Royal
When I googled this shop later, I found it had just opened in December 2023 (^0^;) As usual, no research (^0^;)
Perhaps because it had just opened, even on a weekday lunchtime it was bustling with local customers, and quite a few were in school uniforms (junior high? high school?) 😄
And I was surprised when I went inside! With apologies, the location is rather countryside-like by Okinawa standards, and the quite stylish interior seemed out of place in the area? (🙏 sorry)
I thought it was a stylish interior just like “OKINAWA SOBA HITOTSU” in Wakasa, Naha 😆
Inside there is a ticket machine, and a staff member guided me to buy a ticket. Since it’s a new shop, I’d like them to also introduce cashless payment; unfortunately it seems to be cash only (^0^;)
I ordered the “Royal Soba,” which shares the shop’s name, and waited at the counter seat the staff showed me to 😄
New Royal’s Okinawa soba “How to Eat Course”

When I sat at the counter, there was an explanation called the “How to Eat Course.” The note “Please post it on social media freely” is something new that other shops don’t have, lol. The owner seems to be skilled at marketing that makes full use of social media 😁
If customers who come to eat promote the shop themselves, it will spread through word of mouth as free advertising — impressive, a strategy that matches the present day.

I also try my best to share information on my soba blog and X, so I would have loved to photograph the stylish interior in all sorts of ways, but it was crowded, and there were many young students too, and I’d be embarrassed if an old guy snapping away with a smartphone put people off and I worried about it, so I held back and couldn’t photograph the inside of the shop. Sorry 🙏😆
Menu (I ordered the Royal Soba this time, but the seared braised pork belly rice bowl looks delicious too 😆)
Royal soba　¥950

The “Royal Soba” has arrived 😁 I also learned this later by googling, but a small bowl of mozuku is served first, and I enjoyed it; this shop apparently used to be a mozuku shop and then opened an Okinawa soba shop.
Okinawa soba × mozuku reminds me of “Chodegwa” in Nishihara Town 😆
Recalling that, first I took my usual sip of the broth 😄

It’s a blended broth of bonito and pork bone, with the pork-bone stock coming through, a light and gentle type of pork-bone stock. I thought the flavor of the broth was about the same as shops with an ordinary pork-bone stock.
The noodles aren’t visible in the photo, but they’re medium-thick and apparently use fresh noodles; they were slurpy, but not very firm and relatively soft.

As for the toppings, the braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) is sliced quite thin, which is different from other shops. The pork spare ribs (soki) are tender, but a little sinewy and there were dry spots too.

At the shops I’d eaten at so far, the yushi-dofu used “Unashi Tofu” of Itoman City, but this time, the shop being in Uruma City, they said they use yushi-dofu from the local Uruma City “Shirin-gawa Tofu.”
But sorry 🙏 I have a dull tongue and couldn’t really tell the difference between “Unashi Tofu” and Shirin-gawa Tofu. The Shirin-gawa Tofu yushi-dofu I had this time seemed a little firmer?
New Royal’s flavor-changing condiments
After enjoying the Royal Soba as served, I enjoyed changing the flavor as described in the “How to Eat Course” 😄
On the table were these condiments: ichimi chili, pickled red ginger, yuzu pepper, umai-ume, shikuwasa vinegar, and kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori).
First I added a little “umai-ume” and tasted the noodles and broth. I tried it wondering “does plum paste go with pork-bone stock and Okinawa soba?” but I was surprised (°°)
It was an ordinary pork-bone-stock broth, but it was changed into a refreshing broth with a hint of sourness and noodles with a new taste 😁 It goes well, delicious.

Next I added “shikuwasa vinegar” to the broth. This too changed the ordinary pork-bone-stock broth into a light broth with a hint of sourness. It reminded me of the lemongrass broth at “Kissa Jan” in Yaese Town that I ate a few days ago. However, Jan is bonito-based and this is pork-bone-based, so the flavors differ.

Rating (9/15): It’s just plain tasty. As it’s a newly opened shop, I really hope they go cashless. The interior is stylish and welcoming to social media, so I recommend it to anyone who wants to post photogenic content. The flavor-change approach, using original condiments on a pork-bone-forward broth, feels new. The braised pork belly is thinly sliced, and the soki, though tender, is a little dry and sinewy.

わらまる商店.name: Waramaru Shoten
わらまる商店.desc: A shop that sells itself on being additive-free. An additive-free broth of Makurazaki-grown flower bonito and Hokkaido kelp with sun-dried salt, and plump fresh noodles aged 24 hours. The Kinnikuman-style illustrations on the wall are fun too. A shop featured in Ageage Meshi.
t: * This article was created with AI (Chat GPT 4o) and partly supplemented by me 😁
I ate here in November 2024 😆
I visited a stamp rally participating shop for the first time in a while 😊
This time I visited “Waramaru Shoten” in Osato, Nanjo City.
Waramaru Shoten
It’s a calm-looking shop on the first floor of an apartment building, and the hand-drawn sign and noren reading “Okinawa soba, additive-free” are its landmarks 🏮
It seems to sell itself on being additive-free
The entrance of Waramaru Shoten
At the entrance is displayed the phrase “Open and going strong today!”, conveying a lively atmosphere ✨
The ticket machine installed near the entrance inside the shop
The ticket machine installed near the entrance inside the shop
The ticket machine installed near the entrance inside the shop
The ticket machine installed near the entrance inside the shop (it seems it was featured in Ageage Meshi)
First I bought a “Waramaru Soba (large)” for ¥1,150 at the ticket machine. The machine also says “Our noodles are fresh noodles,” which raises expectations 🍜
After a while the “Waramaru Soba” was brought out, and it exudes gentleness just by its looks 😊
Waramaru soba, large　¥1,150

The broth is, I was told, an additive-free stock combining flower bonito from Makurazaki, Kagoshima Prefecture and kelp from Hokkaido, with sun-dried salt added. When you take a sip, the umami spreads gently and soaks into your body. It’s very light, and you can enjoy a natural flavor 🌿
Explanation panel about the special soba
Waramaru soba, large　¥1,150

The noodles are medium-thin, slightly wavy, aged fresh noodles. Rested for 24 hours or more, these noodles have a plump and slurpy texture with a nice feel going down, and they go well with the broth ✨
The toppings are braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), fish cake (kamaboko), shredded egg, yushi-dofu, and chopped green onions.

The braised pork belly and soft-bone pork ribs are lightly seasoned and both are simmered until melt-in-your-mouth tender, though with a faint sinewy texture. The yushi-dofu adds mellowness and ties everything together gently 😊
As I ate on, I enjoyed changing the flavor with pickled red ginger, shichimi, and kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori) 🌶️
The spicy kick of kōrēgūsu goes well with the light broth, and the pickled red ginger makes a nice accent too 😉
Illustration painted on the wall inside the shop
There is an Ageage Meshi sign on the wall inside the shop
Illustration painted on the wall inside the shop

On the walls inside the shop are hand-drawn Kinnikuman-style illustrations, making it a fun space with a bit of playfulness 🎨 There were also notices that convey the shop’s sincerity, such as their commitment to being additive-free, the use of rice oil and sesame oil for cooking oil, and the use of soft water 💛
Lastly, I made sure to get the stamp rally stamp 📸♪
In this second round of the stamp rally, I only visit shops I haven’t been to 😄

Overall, the broth had more flavor than Shuri-style Okinawa soba, yet its light and gentle taste was memorable. Personally, though, I’d be happier with a bit more punch. Even so, it’s a bowl in which you can feel the commitment to ingredients and a body-friendly finish 😊
Rating (9/15): It’s just plain tasty. When you come to Nanjo City, why not give it a try once?

３丁目の島そば屋.name: San-chome no Shima Soba-ya
３丁目の島そば屋.desc: A shop with queues that bills itself as “No. 1 Okinawa soba in the Central and Northern area.” The broth of bonito, kelp, and dried small sardines with house-made salt tare is a gem on par with a recommended-shop level. The blend of thick, thin, and randomly cut noodles is distinctive too. Comes with jushi and pickles as a free service.
t: I ate here in November 2023. This shop is a participating shop in the “13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (2023.10.1–2024.2.29),” and I went as the 22nd of 34 shops 😊
San-chome no Shima Soba-ya

When I got there, perhaps because it was a holiday lunchtime, there was a huge line (*_*) Moreover, the sign installed above advertises, although the text is cut off in the photo, “No. 1 Okinawa soba ranking in the Central and Northern area.” What confidence, but it does raise my expectations 🤗

The stamp rally booklet featured the “Shima soba,” so I had planned to order that, but looking at the menu at the shop entrance, it was introduced as “Our recommendation!!” and “Most popular No. 1,” which raised my expectations even more, lol
Menu posted at the entrance

Another explanation says the noodles are a “delicate balance blend of thick noodles, thin noodles, and randomly cut noodles.” These are new noodles not found at other shops. The broth is also described as “a light bonito stock that concentrates the umami of natural ingredients.” I like bonito-based broth, so I’m looking forward to it 😁
Explanation posted at the entrance

After a while, my number was called and I went inside. I ordered the “Shima soba (regular).” Payment was prepaid at the table (cash only). There was also a ticket machine at the entrance, but it seemed to be broken and out of use.
Shima soba (regular)　¥850 (jushi and pickles are a free service)
It came with pickles and jushi as a service 😊 Quite a decent portion. First, as always, a sip of the broth.

The broth is made with bonito, kelp, and dried small sardines with house-made salt tare added. You can tell it was carefully prepared. It’s finished as an incredibly delicious broth. I thought this broth is at the level of a recommended shop.
Shima soba (regular)　¥850 (jushi and pickles are a free service)

Next, the noodles blended from various types. When ordering I was asked “Would you like the noodles firm or soft?” and since they recommended firm, I ordered firm. They explained that as I eat, the extra boiling effect makes it just right in the second half.

When I ate it, it was a bit firm, but compared with the firm noodles at other shops I didn’t find it all that firm. The noodles are a blend of various kinds, which you can tell by looks, but the difference wasn’t all that noticeable in the actual eating feel. The noodles are delicious, but I thought they were ordinary.

The toppings include soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), fairly large cuts. The seasoning is somewhere between strong and light. It’s just plain tasty, but the braised pork belly was a bit firm.

Rating (10.5/15): I thought the broth was at a very high level. It’s recommended-shop level. However, the noodles, though a new blend not found at other shops, were just plain tasty. The braised pork belly topping was also a bit firm, but since it’s a popular shop with queues, please do try this shop at least once 🤗

沖縄そば にいぶんじゃ～.name: Okinawa Soba Niibunja~
沖縄そば にいぶんじゃ～.desc: A popular shop in Noborikawa with a cute pink noren. You can choose between fresh noodles kneaded with bonito powder and wavy noodles, and the blended broth of bonito, pork, and chicken is unique. Changing the flavor with the special garlic condiment is fun too.
t: * This article was created with AI (Chat gpt4o) and partly supplemented by me, lol
I ate here in October 2024 😄 This time I’ll introduce my experience at “Okinawa Soba Niibunja~,” which is also listed as a stamp rally participating shop.
From the moment I arrived at the shop, I felt a comforting atmosphere. The exterior's pink noren is striking, and its cute design catches the eye ✨.
Okinawa Soba Niibunja~
Outdoor menu
A warm appearance that conveys how loved it is by the locals ❤️. Inside, the wooden interior feels warm and clean, and a homey atmosphere spreads further.
Inside the shop (it's new)
It was a weekday lunchtime, but the shop was almost full of what seemed to be local regulars! It makes me think this is a really popular shop, and my expectations grew ☺️.
Menu
You can choose from 2 types of noodles 😄
There are also good-value meal tickets

What I ordered this time was the “Mixed Soba” introduced in the stamp rally booklet. At this shop you can choose the noodles from two types, “straight fresh noodles” and “wavy noodles,” and I chose the “straight fresh noodles.” Looking at the menu, it said bonito powder is kneaded into the noodles, which is a somewhat unusual feature ⚡️. When the soba was brought out, the noodles had a faint brownish tint, indeed a different look from ordinary Okinawa soba.
Mixed soba, large　¥1,000

As for the broth, it blends three kinds of stock: bonito, pork, and chicken. No single stock stands out, and it has a mysterious flavor. It’s a unique broth you can’t easily find at other shops, and I felt this is the individuality of “Niibunja~.”
Mixed soba, large　¥1,000

Next, when I took a bite of the noodles, the chewiness and decent firmness were irresistible ❗️. However, although they said bonito powder was kneaded in, honestly I didn't feel much of its flavor. But the quality of the noodles themselves is quite high, and it's a satisfying bowl.

And the toppings are generously piled with braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) ✨. First, the braised pork belly is seasoned very lightly. The soft-bone pork ribs are simmered until tender, and the umami spreads gently with each bite. There's no heaviness at all, so you can eat it refreshingly to the end ♥️.

In addition, a “special garlic” condiment was on the table, and thinking “like ramen,” I added a little. Garlic in Okinawa soba? I wondered, but when I tried it, it was surprisingly good‼️ It offered another way to enjoy it. This condiment seems to be a touch unique to “Niibunja~.”
Special garlic placed as a condiment

All in all, the Okinawa soba at “Niibunja~” cherishes the local flavor while adding its own touches, and what impressed me especially was the chewiness of the noodles and the condiment arrangement ✨. I can well understand why it's loved by the locals. It's a shop I can confidently recommend even to those visiting as tourists.

Rating (9/15): It's just plain tasty. The meal at “Niibunja~” made me appreciate again the depth of Okinawa soba. Next time I'd like to try the “wavy noodles”! I'd also love to try the other menu items ✨✨. Why not give this shop a try too? 😄❤️!

さらばんじ.name: Sarabanji
さらばんじ.desc: A shop on Nago City's east coast, along National Route 331, near Kanucha Bay Resort. A light, gentle bonito broth with medium-thin noodles, and the complimentary small side dishes (kimchi and kubu irichi) are a nice touch too.
t: It was introduced in the "Nago City Soba Map", and I ate here in February 2021 😄
"Sarabanji" along National Route 331 on the east coast side of Nago City
"Sarabanji" introduced as shop 18 of 41 in the "Nago Soba Map"
I ordered the "Soki Soba" introduced in the map
Braised Pork Belly Soba　¥650 (I was supposed to have ordered soki soba but the "Braised Pork Belly Soba" came ^^;)

すば処月桃.name: Suba-dokoro Getto
すば処月桃.desc: A shop with an additive-free stock of ma-kombu kelp, bonito and pork bone, and homemade wood-ash noodles. The smooth, rich pork bone broth is high-level. The specialty is the Shishimai Suba topped with braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) and bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki).
t: I ate here in November 2023. This shop was a participant in the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (2023.10.1–2024.2.29)", and I went as my 23rd of 34 shops 😊
Suba-dokoro Getto (on the 1st floor of a building that looks like a JA building)
This shop wasn't a standalone house; it seemed to be in the 1st floor of a building-like structure. Judging from the address, maybe it's a JA building?
It was lunchtime on a holiday, but when I opened the door and went in, it was completely full (*_*)　I thought this must be a shop really loved by local customers.
But since it's Okinawa soba, I figured turnover would be fast and decided to wait a little. Then several groups left, so I made it inside safely 🤗

For my order, I got the "Shishimai Soba (rich)" introduced in the stamp rally booklet. When I said to the staff, "Nikumai soba, rich please," pointing at the booklet, they replied, "Shishimai soba, rich, right."　I had the reading wrong. In Okinawan dialect, meat is "shishi" (;^ω^)　My apologies lol
Menu
Menu
Menu (explanation part)
While waiting I checked the menu. Apparently these are homemade noodles made using the supernatant of wood ash (lye).
Wood-ash noodles may be a first for me since I had "hijaa (goat) soba" at "Mukashi Mukashi" in Nago.
However, even after a while since ordering, it just wouldn't come; at other shops, even when full, it comes in a reasonable time, but at this shop it just didn't come (;^ω^)
It seems the operation is being run by 2 elderly women, which is tough (;^ω^)
Shishimai Suba (rich) (medium)　¥890
Shishimai Suba (rich) (medium)　¥890

It finally came. First, the broth of course. According to the explanation, the broth: "We carefully make the stock with Hokkaido ma-kombu kelp, bonito and pork bone. The additive-free stock has a deeply nourishing flavor where you can feel savoriness that spreads naturally in your mouth and a powerful richness." 😁

Taking a sip, the rich pork bone stock comes through. It's smooth; I think it's richer and more delicious than the agu-stock Kame Soba or the rich pork bone stock of "Tsukikuruchi" I ate the day before. However, the saltiness is also on the strong side.
I think the broth is smooth, rich and delicious, but as expected it can't beat "796 Nankuru", which I introduce as a recommended shop 😊

Next I have the noodles. They're a medium-thin straight type. According to the explanation, "The homemade wood-ash noodles have a good aroma, and you can feel a springy chewiness, smooth texture going down, and a faint sweetness."
However, when I ate them, I couldn't feel the aroma or flavor of wood ash, and I think the ones I ate before at "Mukashi Mukashi" in Nago City had more flavor.
However, the noodles themselves are smooth and I think plain tasty. These noodles also come across a bit salty.
The toppings have volume with braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) and bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), but the hon-soki had a bit of sinewy texture and felt dry.

Rating (9.5/15): Plain tasty. The pork bone broth is fairly smooth and delicious, but a bit on the salty side. The noodles are smooth and plain tasty too, but these also come across salty. The operation when it's full is a bit disappointing.

そばcafeホウオウボク.name: Soba cafe Hoouboku
そばcafeホウオウボク.desc: A shop in Sokei, Ginoza Village, whose charm is a peaceful atmosphere where time seems to stand still. The signature is the good-value Hoouboku Soba with a chicken, pork and bonito stock broth, thick curly noodles, and jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) included. There are outdoor seats and 2nd-floor seats too, so you can spend your time yonna-yonna (slowly, slowly).
t: I ate here in November 2023. This shop was a participant in the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (2023.10.1–2024.2.29)", and I went as my 20th of 34 shops 😊
Soba cafe Hoouboku (it's in a very peaceful place 😊)
Soba cafe Hoouboku (it's in a very peaceful place 😊)
There are outdoor seats too 😁
This time I ate on the 1st floor, but there seems to be a 2nd floor too.
This shop is in a place called Sokei, Ginoza Village (Ginoza-son Sokei), and it's in a very peaceful location 🤗
When I went, I also felt an atmosphere like time had somehow stopped 😊　It made me feel like, in life, you don't have to rush so much; yonna-yonna (slowly, slowly) is fine lol

It was lunchtime on a weekday, but when I went in there was no one there. The relaxed feel is nice lol　When you enter the front door there's a meal ticket machine, and I ordered the "Hoouboku Soba" introduced in the stamp rally booklet.
Menu (I ordered the Hoouboku Soba introduced in the stamp rally, and it seems jushi comes with it too. What a good deal 🤗)

Seeing the meal ticket machine in front of the entrance, I thought "Cash only, huh," bought my meal ticket from the machine with cash and handed it in at the counter inside, but lo and behold, there was a PayPay QR code reader barcode placed there (;^ω^)　If they accept cashless too, I wish they'd let people know at the entrance (;^ω^)　I probably could have paid with my smartphone, but since I'd already bought the meal ticket with cash, I handed in my Hoouboku Soba ticket without complaint (;^ω^)
Hoouboku Soba (with jushi)　¥850
After a while, the "Hoouboku Soba" I ordered came 😊　Including jushi is great service 😊　First, I taste the broth (lol)
As the menu says, the stock broth using chicken, pork and bonito is a broth where the pork bone comes through somewhat.
Hoouboku Soba (with jushi)　¥850

Next I have the noodles. They're thick curly noodles with a soft feel, and since jushi comes with it too, the volume is full marks. The fish cake (kamaboko) is a topping not found at other shops, with a kind of Okinawan celebratory feel 🤗

Rating (9/15): It's an Okinawa soba shop where you can eat in a mellow atmosphere, at a location where time really seems to have stopped 😊　I recommend it to those who want to eat Okinawa soba leisurely in that kind of atmosphere. How about trying it once?

そば家幸.desc: In Kanna, Ginoza Village, marked by a warehouse-like exterior along National Route 329. A rare shop open only on Saturdays and Sundays, its interior is packed with pro baseball goods such as the Yomiuri Giants. The signature dish is the Sachi Soba with a blended broth where the richness of pork bone comes through. They also ship soba.
t: *This article was created with "ChatGPT 4o" with some additions by me. I went to eat here in January 2025 😄

Sachi Soba (large)　¥950

The bowl that was brought out has a very Okinawan yachimun-style design, and just the look of it gets me excited 🎵　In addition to braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), there's fish cake (kamaboko) on top too, so it has quite a lot of volume. Rating (9/15): All in all, it feels plain tasty 👍　Even if you're not a baseball fan you can enjoy it, but it's a shop I'd really like you to visit once when you come to the northern region during camp season. You might be a little overwhelmed by the number of uniforms and photos on display (lol)

つばめ御茶屋御殿.name: Tsubame Uchaya Udun
つばめ御茶屋御殿.desc: A charming shop named after "Uchaya Udun," a villa of the Ryukyu royal family. In an elegant interior decorated with artworks such as Ryukyu lacquerware and pottery, you can enjoy soki soba made with Kamehama Soba's thin straight noodles.
t: This article was created with AI (ChatGPT 4o), with some additions by me 😁
I went to eat here in November 2024 😄

This time I made my way to "Tsubame Uchaya Udun" in Asato, Naha ✨ The "Uchaya Udun" in the shop's name apparently refers to a villa built for the royal family's guests in the era of the Ryukyu Kingdom 🏯 With a name that sounds so prestigious, I visited wondering what kind of Okinawa soba was waiting for me 😋

Opening the menu, there's a simple yet carefully selected lineup of Okinawa soba 🍜 From it, this time I ordered the "Soki Soba" 🎶 At ¥1,200 the price is set a bit high, but if they're particular about their craft, it's an understandable price range 💰
Soki suba ¥1200

After waiting a while, an elegant-looking soki soba was brought to the red lacquered table 🍲 The broth is a stock combining pork bone, bonito flakes, and kelp, and taking a sip, it's finished with a balance where neither the bonito nor the pork bone asserts itself too much ✨ However, personally I might have liked one of them to assert itself a little more 🤔
Soki suba ¥1200

The noodles are Kamehama Soba's thin straight noodles, which are rare for Okinawa soba 🍜 These have a unique texture, going down smooth and slippery, and when you bite them you can enjoy a moderate springiness 😆 They give a clean, refreshing impression.

And then, the main pork spare ribs (soki). They look big and seem thoroughly simmered, but when I took a bite, the seasoning was on the light side, and the slightly dry texture bothered me 🤔 Since I'd been expecting soki that's tender and falls apart, it was a bit of a letdown 💦 With less fat, some people might find them easy to eat, but personally I wanted them a bit juicier 😅

Overall, the shop's atmosphere and the quality of the noodles are high, but my impression was that the soki's preparation was a bit of a shame 😌 You can enjoy a leisurely meal in the calm space inside, so it might be the perfect shop to drop by between sightseeing stops 🏖️

Rating (9/15): Overall, I'd call it a "decently tasty Okinawa soba" 😋 If it had a few more distinctive points, it would probably be an even more memorable bowl ✨ I'm looking forward to my next Okinawa soba tour too ♪🥢

てんtoてん.name: Ten to Ten
てんtoてん.desc: A hideaway with a hugely impactful exterior completely covered in vines. For Okinawa soba, it stakes everything on mokkai soba (made with wood-ash lye) alone. A gentle bonito-based flavor, and changing it up with kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori) is fun too.
t: I heard from an acquaintance that it was good, and went to eat there in July 2022 😄
After getting a bit lost, I found the shop in a residential area lol
Ten to Ten in a residential area (it has a huge visual impact ^^;)
It's completely covered in vines lol. Amazing lol
I relied on my map app and went into a residential area, but when I arrived I was stunned (・・)
Thinking, "Wow, what an amazing look," I went in as the first customer of the day.
Menu (for Okinawa soba, they stake everything on just one kind: "mokkai soba")
They're going all-in with "mokkai soba" as the only choice. Of course I ordered the mokkai soba lol
Mokkai soba (made with wood-ash lye) ¥700

A sip of the broth. ?? It's a gentle bonito-based flavor, but to me it tasted very weak. Also, the mokkai soba noodles didn't have the flavor I'd tasted at other shops, and they felt the same as ordinary noodles to me.

Rating (8.5/15): Unlike the striking exterior, the soba itself was weak in flavor overall and left me unsatisfied. I was the first customer of the day, so maybe the bonito broth hadn't been fully extracted yet? ^^; Partway through I added kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori) to change up the flavor and ate it that way.

でいご家.name: Deigo-ya
でいご家.desc: An Okinawa soba set-meal shop that's easy to find along National Route 58 in Kise, Nago. Thin straight noodles in a gentle bonito-based broth, with tender soft-bone pork ribs. Changing up the flavor with kōrēgūsu is great too.
t: It isn't listed on the "Nago City Soba Map" that got me started on my Okinawa soba tour, but it's easy to find along National Route 58 in Kise, Nago, so I gave it a try ☺
Deigo-ya (along National Route 58 in Kise, Nago)
Soft-bone pork rib (nankotsu soki) soba ¥880

I ordered the "Soft-Bone Pork Rib Soba." Thin, straight noodles in a gentle bonito-based broth. The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) are tender and tasty 😋 After drinking about half the broth, I enjoyed changing up the flavor by adding kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori) lol. The chili really kicks in.
Rating (9/15): It's decently tasty. The location on National Route 58 is easy to find too, so why not give it a try?

なかざ家.name: Nakaza-ya
なかざ家.desc: A shop with a huge impact from its white, rich pork bone broth and white ginger. Adding their homemade "Buta-gusu" (instead of kōrēgūsu) changes the flavor to savory-spicy and makes it even tastier. The No. 1 most popular dish is the seared soft-bone pork rib soba.
t: I went here in December 2022 😄
Nakaza-ya (rich pork bone is their selling point)
Looking at the menu, I ordered the "Seared Soft-Bone Pork Rib Soba," introduced as the No. 1 most popular dish 😁
Ordered the No. 1 most popular dish (seared soft-bone pork rib soba) from the menu
Their specialty: apparently "Buta-gusu" instead of kōrēgūsu. At this point I was already looking forward to changing up the flavor partway through lol
The No. 1 most popular seared soft-bone pork rib soba ¥980

The white broth has impact lol. Plus, instead of pickled red ginger, there's white ginger, which other shops don't have. A sip of the broth. It looks rich, but it's surprisingly light. The noodles are chewy, medium-thin noodles, and the seared soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) are well seasoned through and tasty 😋
After eating about half, I added the "Buta-gusu" I'd been looking forward to and changed up the flavor.
The light broth changed to savory-spicy, and it got even tastier.

Rating (9/15): Personally, I found the broth too light as it was, so it was tastier after adding the "Buta-gusu." I thought maybe the broth is made on the assumption that you'll add Buta-gusu. Other shops don't have a white broth, so please be sure to give this one a try too 😄

なかむらそば.name: Nakamura Soba
なかむらそば.desc: Provisional #2 (13.5/15). A popular shop along National Route 58 where you can enjoy your soba while gazing at the sea. The specialty "Asa Soba," with sea lettuce (āsa) kneaded into the noodles and fish cake, is a must-eat. The jumbo braised pork belly soba is limited to 7 servings a day.
t: At first I was touring Okinawa soba shops within Nago, but after seeing it introduced as delicious on social media, I went to "Nakamura Soba" in Onna Village along National Route 58 (November 2022).
"Nakamura Soba" in Onna Village, which I consider delicious at provisional #2. It's along National Route 58, so you'll find it right away
This is also a popular shop where a line forms quickly, so I went early. I somehow managed to get inside without getting caught in the line lol

I ordered the "Asa Soba" recommended in the shop. Sea lettuce (āsa) is a staple in Okinawa. Sea lettuce miso soup, clear soup, and sea lettuce tempura are delicious too. To begin with, "āsa" is what Okinawans call the seaweed "hitoegusa." It clings to rocks in the shallows along Okinawa's coast, and it seems it's in season and delicious from February to May.

It's rich in dietary fiber, minerals, and calcium, and in particular contains plenty of beta-carotene, so it seems effective for anti-aging and cancer prevention. Apparently it has about 8 times the calcium of milk and about twice the folic acid of spinach (according to information in the shop). Maybe this is the source of the old-time Uchinanchu (Okinawans) being No. 1 in longevity? lol
"Nakamura Soba" is particular about sea lettuce, so maybe you'll live a long, healthy life? lol

First, a sip of the broth. This one also has plenty of bonito-based stock coming through and is tasty. The moment I drank it, it had a deliciousness unlike any shop I'd been to so far. The noodles are thin, and sea lettuce is kneaded into both the noodles and the fish cake (kamaboko), a creative touch and deliciousness not found at other shops. The braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) was also tender and delicious. I thought the balance of broth, noodles, and toppings ranked near the top among all the Okinawa soba shops I'd eaten at so far.
Nakamura Soba's recommended Asa Soba (medium) ¥800

I ate by the window, so it was Okinawa soba while looking at the sea ✌ When the weather is good, the sea in Onna Village turns a beautiful emerald green, so if your timing is right, both the taste and the view will be the best.
The view from the seat where I ate this time. If the weather cooperates, you can see the beautiful emerald-green sea of Onna Village right in front of you.

Rating (13.5/15): Well, for now I'm ranking each shop, but it's not like there's a huge difference in taste, and there's personal preference too, so I think it's only a hair behind #1. This time I had the "Asa Soba," but next time I want to try the "Jumbo Braised Pork Belly Soba, limited to 7 servings a day" that was on the sign outside 🤤 It seems you won't be able to get it unless you go early.

なんごく食堂.name: Nangoku Shokudo
なんごく食堂.desc: An old-fashioned local diner along National Route 331. Its appeal is the value: soki soba for ¥700 with complimentary rice containing fish sausage. It comes with unusual Yaeyama fish cake. There's a spacious parking lot too.
t: I went to "Nangoku Shokudo" in Komesu, Itoman, on my Okinawa soba tour 🌺🍜 I ate here in March 2025 😄
Nangoku Shokudo

The shop had red banners out along the road, so even from a distance it had that "Ah, this must be it" feel 🚗✨ The exterior doesn't look new; it has the weathered look of an old-fashioned diner, and the sign is a little faded too, which gives it plenty of local character. Shops like this get me a little excited even before I go in 😊
Parking lot in front of the shop

The parking lot is quite spacious, and it's a nice plus that it's easy to get to by car 🅿️ The Komesu area of Itoman has a quiet, laid-back atmosphere different from the bustle of tourist spots, and it felt like I'd come to an old-fashioned Okinawan neighborhood diner 🌿 Red "Open" banners and "Okinawa Soba" banners were swaying in the wind, so even from outside it really had the atmosphere of a diner.
Inside the shop
Inside the shop

Inside, table seats are lined up in a fairly spacious room, and it felt like a place where you can sit comfortably. With blue chairs, wood-grain tables, a TV on the wall, self-serve water, and an old-fashioned air, it feels less like a shop built for tourists and more like a place where locals come for their everyday lunch 📺🍵 There's also an aquarium and plants inside, and it was nice that time seemed to flow somehow leisurely 🐟🌱 It's not flashy, but I don't dislike the air of a simple diner like this.
Menu posted on the wall

The menu was posted on the wall and included Okinawa soba, soki soba, meat soba, vegetable soba, zenzai, taco rice, tempura soba, katsu soba, and more 📄 Prices like ¥600 for Okinawa soba and ¥700 for soki soba feel very reasonable considering the times 💰 This time I ordered the soki soba, and it's nice that complimentary rice comes with it 🍚 What's more, that rice isn't just plain white rice; it has little chopped pieces of fish sausage in it. I'd hardly ever seen this at other shops, and it had an amusing original touch 😳
Soki soba ¥700

The soki soba that was brought out looked simple, but it had pork spare ribs (soki), green onions, fish cake (kamaboko), and also Yaeyama fish cake 🍜✨ Yaeyama fish cake on Okinawa soba felt quite rare to me. It's a topping you don't often see at other shops, so this left a bit of an impression. Just having the rounded Yaeyama fish cake instead of regular fish cake gave it a little personality in looks, too.

The broth is pork-bone-based 🐷 It does have a gentle, diner-style flavor, but it didn't have much of the pull that makes you think, "I want to eat this again soon." To be honest, my impression was that the broth was pretty ordinary.
Soki soba ¥700

The noodles are medium-thin, wavy flat noodles 🥢 As you can see in the photo, they're the type that's a bit flat with a loose wave. The texture is on the soft side. I prefer a bit more chewiness and springiness 🍜 My impression here was also that they're ordinary.

The soki was on the light side 🍖 Rather than being thoroughly soaked in a sweet-savory flavor and meltingly tender, it had a simple, restrained seasoning; if the flavor were soaked in a bit more and the meat's savoriness came forward more, I think the impression of the whole bowl would improve. The Yaeyama fish cake was unusual and nice, but looking at the toppings as a whole, they didn't move me all that much.

The complimentary rice with chopped fish sausage in it is truly unique 🍚🌭 Taste-wise, rather than being very special, it's homey and simple. Eaten together with the soba it fills you up properly, so considering you get soki soba and rice for ¥700, the value isn't bad 👍 However, even including the rice, my overall impression still settled on "it's ordinary."

Rating (9/15): I think Nangoku Shokudo is less the type of famous shop that leaves a strong impression with the polish of its flavor, and more a shop for enjoying the atmosphere of an old-fashioned local diner 🌺 The relaxed interior, spacious parking lot, reasonable prices, and complimentary rice were all good points 😊 However, if you ask whether it's worth making a special trip from far away for an Okinawa soba tour, I'd say not quite. It did have personality with the Yaeyama fish cake and the rice with fish sausage, but the noodles, broth, and toppings were all average, and overall it felt like a bowl for everyday use 🍜✨

なーざと家.name: Nazato-ya
なーざと家.desc: Diagonally across from Miyazato Junior High, a no-nonsense shop that stakes everything on just two dishes: soft-bone pork rib soba and braised pork belly soba. A pork- and chicken-based broth with plenty of bonito stock, plus meltingly tender soft-bone pork ribs. There's even an autograph from announcer Azumi.

Nazato-ya (diagonally across from Miyazato Junior High)
Looking at the menu, there are only two kinds of Okinawa soba: "Soft-Bone Pork Rib Soba" and "Braised Pork Belly Soba." Going all-in with a small menu is cool 😊
Menu

Soft-bone pork rib (nankotsu soki) soba (medium) ¥700

The pork- and chicken-based broth has plenty of bonito stock coming through and is tasty 😋 The noodles are the thin type, and the soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) are meltingly tender and delicious. It seems to have been featured in the media too; it's an old one, but an autograph from announcer Azumi of the show Pittanko Kan Kan was on display 😄
All sorts of autographs were on display

ぴぱら.name: Pipara
ぴぱら.desc: An Okinawa soba shop in the food court of "Onna no Eki Nakayukui Market," bustling with tourists. The braised pork belly soba, with thin noodles in a broth of rich pork bone and plenty of bonito stock, is popular. The photo spot with a view of Iejima Tatchu and browsing the local-produce souvenirs are fun too.
t: *I had AI (Claude Opus 4.1) help write this article too, and I've added and updated parts of it myself lol. I ate here in December 2024 😄

This time I'd like to introduce "Pipara," an Okinawa soba shop inside "Onna no Eki Nakayukui Market" in Nakadomari, Onna Village. This is a tourist facility whose concept is "a village farmers' market that connects people with people," and it's a popular spot that's always bustling with lots of tourists 🌺
Signs set up in the Onna no Eki parking lot

When you pull into the Onna no Eki parking lot, the first thing that leaps into view is a set of signs with cute bitter melon (goya) and pineapple characters drawn on them. Greetings in the Okinawan dialect like "Matan, mensore" (come again, welcome) are written on them too, which gets tourists excited 😊 The weather was nice that day too, with blue skies spreading out, perfect for sightseeing ☀️
Onna no Eki
Onna no Eki

Inside the facility, it has exactly the atmosphere of a roadside station, with local farm produce, seafood, souvenirs, and more lined up in rows. Among them, our destination this time, "Okinawa Soba Pipara," had its shop in the food court area. Actually, there were other shops like a seafood bowl shop too, and everything looked so delicious I didn't know where to look 😋
Okinawa Soba Pipara
Okinawa Soba Pipara

When you stand in front of Pipara's ticket machine, there's a long row of menu items with photos. Among them, I decided to order the "Braised Pork Belly Soba," which was introduced as a "popular item."
Ticket machine
Onna no Eki also has a photo spot
Iejima Tatchu on the horizon (you can see it when the weather is good)

Outside Onna no Eki, the beautiful Okinawan sea spreads out 🌊 On days with good weather, you can even see Iejima's Tatchu (Gusuku-yama) in the distance. There's also a photo spot 📸, and from the photo spot at the top of the slope you can take great scenic shots 😄

After a while my number was called, and I picked up the "Braised Pork Belly Soba" at the counter. In the bowl are neatly arranged braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), thin noodles, green onions, and a broth with a bit of extra oil floating on top. First, as always, let's taste the broth 😊
Braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) soba ¥1,000

Taking a sip of the broth, you can feel the richness of the pork bone, but the bonito stock comes through too. However, my impression was that it was a little on the oily side. Still, it's decently tasty in its own way. After walking around in the Okinawan heat, this richer broth actually feels like it soaks right into your body.
Braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) soba ¥1,000

Next, the noodles. They're thin noodles with a loose wave, and the texture is on the soft side. They cling well to the broth and slip down easily. They feel like gentle noodles with no quirks that even tourists will find easy to eat 🍜

And as for the braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) topping, it had a sweet seasoning that was well soaked in. However, some parts still had a bit of sinewy texture, so it was finished with more chewiness than melting tenderness. The sweet-savory seasoning feels like classic Okinawa soba, and I think it's a flavor that even tourists eating Okinawa soba for the first time will find easy to like.
After eating, as I strolled around the facility, there were lots of fresh seafood and local vegetables for sale, so you can enjoy picking out souvenirs too 🎁
Souvenir corner inside Onna no Eki

When you step outside the facility, the contrast between the blue sea and sky is truly beautiful, and a quintessentially Okinawan view spreads out before you. You can see the sea from the parking lot too, so being able to soak up the Okinawa vibe from the moment you get out of the car is a nice plus ✨
There's also an Onna Village tourist map

"Onna no Eki" feels like an ordinary roadside station, but I think it's a good spot for tourists to casually experience Okinawan food and culture. Besides Okinawa soba, you can enjoy all kinds of Okinawan food like seafood bowls and taco rice, so it's the perfect place to drop by during a break on a drive 😄

Rating (9/15): Pipara's Okinawa soba this time isn't especially distinctive, but it has the steady deliciousness you'd expect from a tourist spot, and it felt decently tasty. When you visit Onna Village for sightseeing, why not stop by once as a nice spot to enjoy Okinawa soba while gazing at the beautiful sea 🌴

まいにち食堂.name: Mainichi Shokudo
まいにち食堂.desc: A popular shop in Kina, Yomitan Village, that's also been featured on NHK. Housed in the renovated first floor of an apartment building, it serves a rich, bonito-based broth with no chemical seasonings and meltingly tender soft-bone pork ribs. The mugwort-flavored fuchiba shichimi spice is distinctive too. A line forms at lunchtime.
t: It was featured on an NHK program, and I went to eat there in September 2022.
"Mainichi Shokudo" The first floor of an ordinary residential apartment building has been renovated into the shop
Soft-bone pork rib (nankotsu soki) soba ¥800

Rating (9/15): It was decently tasty, but the NHK program said something like they can even make kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori) specially for each individual, so I thought it might taste different from other shops, but with the one placed in the shop I couldn't tell the difference from the usual kōrēgūsu. まるひら食堂.name: Maruhira Shokudo

t: The shop I'm introducing this time is "Maruhira Shokudo" in Uka, Kunigami Village, at the northernmost tip of Okinawa's main island. This shop is actually a place with history that has long been loved by locals as the former Uka Community Store 😁 I went to eat there in December 2024; it's been featured in the newspaper too and is known as "the northernmost diner on Okinawa's west coast."
Maruhira Shokudo

Since it's in Kunigami Village at the very north of Okinawa's main island, it's not a place you can easily come to, but that's exactly what makes it feel special ✨ When you step inside, there's the atmosphere of an old-fashioned diner. Since it was lunchtime, surprisingly there were quite a lot of customers 😲 Maybe it's not just locals but lots of people visiting on sightseeing trips too.
Menu posted inside the shop

Looking at the menu posted on the wall, there's a wide selection of set meals besides Okinawa soba. I'm especially curious about the dish called "Genkotsu Set Meal" 😆 It apparently comes with super-huge fried chicken, and it seems to be a famous dish too. This time the goal was my Okinawa soba tour, so I decided to order the "Braised Pork Belly Soba, Medium" from the menu. At ¥750 the price is reasonable too, and though you can't tell from the menu, it's a nice plus that pickles come complimentary 😊
Menu
Braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) soba, medium ¥750

After ordering and waiting a while, the "Braised Pork Belly Soba" was brought out. It looks simple, but it feels like a proper Okinawa soba. First, as always, I'll taste the broth 😋 The pork-bone-based broth has a gentle, light flavor. The not-too-strong pork bone flavor is pleasant, and it's finished as a homey taste that somehow feels nostalgic. Maybe because of its northernmost location, it has a gentle seasoning that tourists can easily take to.

Next, the noodles. They're wavy noodles with a softish texture. The braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) topping is sliced thin like ramen chashu and is very tender. It's a different texture from thick braised pork belly, and it's tasty in its own way ✨ It's topped with plenty of finely shredded white leek too, and its crunchy texture is a nice accent.

The appeal of Maruhira Shokudo is, above all, the special feeling of it being "the northernmost tip of Okinawa's main island." Okinawa soba eaten after coming all the way to Kunigami Village, where an ordinary Okinawa soba tour rarely takes you, becomes an experience that stays in your memory even more than the taste 😊 Being a former community store, it has a warm atmosphere rooted in the community, with a charm different from Okinawa soba shops in urban areas. Eating Okinawa soba while time flows leisurely makes you forget the busyness of daily life.

Also, as the newspaper coverage shows, this shop is an important presence supporting the local food culture. It's a shop I'd definitely like you to drop by when you visit the northern region on a sightseeing trip 😄 The taste was decently good. It's not exceptionally outstanding in flavor, but I think the shop's big appeal is its northernmost location, its history as a former community store, and the warm atmosphere of a place that continues to be loved by the community ✨
It's been featured in the newspaper too, as "Local flavor at the northernmost tip"

Rating (9/15): When you come to sightsee in the northern region or enjoy the nature of Yanbaru, please be sure to try the Okinawa soba here at Maruhira Shokudo. You can have the special experience of "the northernmost Okinawa soba" that you can't usually taste 😊 Next time I'm also curious about the super-huge fried chicken of the "Genkotsu Set Meal," so if I get the chance I'd like to give it a try 😆

I went to eat here in June 2024 😄 Using the ¥500 discount voucher for Miyo-ya that I received at the Soba Jogu awards ceremony for the recent Okinawa soba stamp rally, I went to eat the "Tojin Soba" I'd been curious about for a while 😆
This "Tojin Soba" is said to be the roots of Okinawa soba, and it's a dish revived after 110 years.

Miyo-ya has an eye-catching storefront with colorful, very Okinawan decorations, and at the entrance hangs a sign reading "Homemade Noodles Okinawa Soba." As always, it was bustling with local customers.
Miyo-ya
You order easily inside the shop, receive a number tag, and wait at your seat. The wait wasn't that long, and the staff were kind and pleasant.
Number slip and order receipt 😄 (When I had ChatGPT read this photo, it recognized it as a "number tag" and wrote the article above. Amazing (^0^;))

Inside the shop, there's a poster explaining the history and features of "Tojin Soba" in detail. "Tojin Soba" can be called the origin of Okinawa soba, and this soba, revived after roughly 110 years, is characterized by its special soy-sauce-based broth.
Poster inside the shop explaining "Tojin Soba," the roots of Okinawa soba
Poster inside the shop explaining "Tojin Soba," the roots of Okinawa soba
Tojin soba ¥800

The "Tojin Soba" that was brought out is striking just from the look of its black broth. Taking a sip, I expected a strong soy sauce flavor, but it was a gentle taste with plenty of bonito flavor coming through. This is an irresistible point for lovers of Okinawa soba with bonito-based broth.
Tojin soba ¥800

Next, the noodles. The homemade fresh noodles have a chewy texture and go perfectly with the broth. This chewiness is something special you can't get with store-bought noodles, and they're satisfying to eat.

The toppings include green onions and tofu-sized chunks of pork, letting you enjoy a flavor a little different from regular Okinawa soba. The flavor of this meat combined with the broth gave the whole bowl a very good balance.

"Tojin Soba" is a dish worthy of the word "revival," with the broth, noodles, and toppings each in fine harmony. It was also a nice plus that I could enjoy it for effectively ¥300 using the ¥500 discount voucher. It wasn't just decently tasty; it was a bowl where I could feel history and tradition.

Rating (9/15): The broth looks black and striking, like it would taste strong, but it has the usual Okinawa soba bonito broth coming through and is decently tasty. How about Miyo-ya, where you can taste "Tojin Soba," the roots of Okinawa soba?

First, the soup: the broth made with Agu pork had a very gentle flavor. You can sense the richness of the meat, but it's not heavy, finished to be easy to drink. A comforting flavor that seems likely to appeal to a wide range of ages. It's the same flavor as the other Kame Soba shops 😄
Honke Kame soba ¥890

The noodles are thin and straight, finished on the soft side. The smooth, slippery feel going down is pleasant, and they clung well to the soup. Personally I'd be even happier with a bit more chewiness, but as it is, it's a classic flavor.

And the toppings are mainly soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku). Both are simmered until melt-in-your-mouth, and their tenderness, crumbling apart in your mouth, was appealing. The seasoning is just right too, with a perfectly balanced sweet-savory taste.

Overall, while not flashy, it was a bowl with a reliable flavor. What was especially memorable was the gentleness of the soup. I think it's something that a wide range of people, from Okinawa soba beginners to local regulars, can enjoy.
Rating (9/15): Simply tasty, and you can enjoy the same Kame Soba as at the other shops 😄

亀そば（北中店）.name: Kame Soba (Kitanaka Branch)
亀そば（北中店）.desc: The Kame Soba Kitanaka branch along Route 330. A surprisingly light Agu broth considering how it looks, medium-thin noodles, and tender braised pork belly and rafute. There are also locations in Nishihara Town, Roadside Station Kadena, and Minatomachi in Naha City.
t: I ate here in March 2019 😊
Kame Soba (Kitanaka Branch), along Route 330
Kame soba (medium) ¥600

I ordered the "Kame soba". From the color of the soup it looks like it would be strongly flavored, but the Agu broth is very light. Medium-thin noodles, and the braised pork belly and rafute are tender and delicious 😋

Rating (9/15): Simply tasty. It seems popular with locals, and at lunchtime it was full of customers. There are also Kame Soba shops in Nishihara Town, Roadside Station Kadena, and Minatomachi in Naha City, so how about trying it once?

二見そば.name: Futami Soba
二見そば.desc: A soba shop in a lone house standing along the mountains connecting the east and west of Nago City. Featured on the Nago Soba Map, it's particular about its chicken, pork, and bonito blended broth and homemade kōrēgūsu. The everything-on-top is loaded with toppings and superb. *There are reports it has been closed since around May 2024.
t: It was featured on the "Nago City Soba Map", and I tried it in September 2020 😀
*Please note that as of August 2024 there are reports that this shop is closed (since around May 2024?).
Futami Soba (driving along the mountains between Route 58 on Nago City's west coast and Route 329 on the east coast, it appears like a lone house in the middle of nowhere lol)
The interior is a renovated detached house, with a warm atmosphere like someone's home 😁
I ordered the "Futami soba everything-on-top" featured on the soba map.
"Futami Soba" is featured as shop 23 of 41 on the "Nago Soba Map"
Futami soba everything-on-top (¥850)

Loaded with toppings — pork spare ribs (soki), braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), kombu, and yushi-dofu — it's the best 😁 The medium-thin noodles go well with the soup made from painstakingly prepared chicken, pork, and bonito broth, and it's delicious.
The kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori) is homemade too, and you can tell that everything is made carefully with a great deal of time and effort.
Rating (12/15): Futami Soba is particular about making things in-house. This is also recommended, so please try it.
PS: I don't have a photo, but the actress Meisa Kuroki is apparently from around here, and she seems to like this soba shop too — I think there was her autograph in the shop.

今帰仁そば.name: Nakijin Soba
今帰仁そば.desc: A tile-roofed old-house soba shop near Nakijin Castle Ruins and Churaumi Aquarium. Agu pork and bonito blended broth with homemade noodles, and you can choose from four toppings. The three homemade condiments made with Yanbaru ingredients are fun too, and it's a photogenic spot.
t: I ate here in April 2025 😊 This time, on an Okinawa soba tour of the northern area of the main island, I went to "Nakijin Soba" in Shoshi, Nakijin Village 🌺 Nakijin Village is an area close to the World Heritage site Nakijin Castle Ruins and Churaumi Aquarium, and this shop is in a spot that's easy to drop by while sightseeing 😄
Nakijin Soba

Arriving at the shop, the first thing that jumped out at me was a very Okinawan tile-roofed old house. The noren (shop curtain) with "Nanokuni-mura Style House" and "Nakijin Soba" written in large letters, plus the yellow "Open" sign, really build up the atmosphere ✨ This is exactly what an Okinawan old-house soba shop looks like 😊 Just the exterior gets you excited 🎵
Nakijin Soba

Before you pass under the noren at the entrance, there's a rugged Ryukyu limestone wall, bougainvillea flowers, and trees like banyans planted, giving it a super Okinawan feel 🌴 It had become a photogenic spot that makes tourists want to take pictures 📸
Inside the shop

When you go inside, this too is a stylish design 😲 Stylish rattan chairs and tables are arranged, and it's an open space with natural light coming in through the sudare (bamboo blinds). It keeps the charm of an old house while feeling new 🌸
Inside the shop

Inside there's also a raised tatami area, which has an atmosphere like an old-fashioned Okinawan grandma's house 😊 Orion Beer posters and Nakijin Village watermelon posters are up, so you can feel the local vibe too 🍉
Menu

Looking at the menu, the signature "Nakijin soba" is ¥950. Homemade noodles with Agu pork and bonito broth, and it's set up so you can choose from four toppings 😄 You choose from "melt-in-your-mouth nankotsu soki", "seared salt-flavored sanmai-niku", "mix", and "yushi-dofu (limited quantity)", and this time I greedily ordered the mix (plus ¥50) 🍜 There's also kids' soba (¥750), a Nakijin soba set (¥1,350), jushi (¥300), homemade yushi-dofu (¥400), and more.
Condiments on the table

There are three kinds of condiments on the table — "nama-shichimi (spicy miso made with Yanbaru shikuwasa and island chili peppers)", "nimi togarashi (Yanbaru shikuwasa and island chili peppers)", and "kōrēgūsu" — all homemade condiments made with Yanbaru ingredients, which gets you excited 🌶️ They seem to sell them as souvenirs too, and you can sense their dedication ✨
Nakijin soba (mix) ¥1,000

After a short wait, the Nakijin soba (mix) was brought out 🍜 In a bowl that looks like Uruma ware, it looks very photogenic, with something white and creamy like yushi-dofu, julienned ginger, soft-bone pork ribs, seared braised pork belly, and green onion arranged in good balance 😊

The customary sip of soup. It's supposed to be an Agu pork and bonito blended broth, but hmm, honestly it's a light style where neither really comes through 🤔 Not in a bad way — it's a very gentle flavor with a refined finish — but personally I thought it'd be fine if the richness of the Agu pork or the bonito aroma hit a bit harder. Maybe they've finished it to have broad appeal for tourists 😅
Nakijin soba (mix) ¥1,000
Next I have the noodles 🍜 Homemade medium-thick, gently wavy noodles, and these are pretty good 😋 They have solid chewiness, and the noodles are simply tasty 👍

The braised pork belly and soft-bone pork ribs toppings are simmered until melt-in-your-mouth and tender, but my impression was that for the price of ¥1,000, they were a bit on the small side 😅 And some parts of the soft-bone pork ribs still had a bit of a sinewy texture, so I'd have been happier if they were just a little more fall-apart tender 🥩

Rating (9/15): The charming old-house exterior and the stylishly renovated interior are outstanding, and it seems like a shop that will be popular with tourists 😊 But as for the flavor, honestly, it's "ordinary" 🤔 With a light soup where neither the Agu pork nor the bonito comes through, and toppings on the small side for ¥1,000, I'd say it needs a little more in terms of value for money 🍜 For those who want to enjoy the atmosphere of an old house on the way back from sightseeing in Nakijin Village or from Churaumi Aquarium, I think it's worth stopping by 😄

喫茶ジャーン.name: Kissa Jaan

嘉海食堂.name: Kakai Shokudo
嘉海食堂.desc: A popular diner along National Route 329 in Yaka, Kin Town. The Kakai Soba, limited to 10 servings a day, is topped with everything—pig's feet (tebichi), pork spare ribs (soki), braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), kelp, egg, and fish cake (kamaboko)—plus okara on the side, for a very generous portion. The "first in Japan" pig's feet (tebichi) vending machine in front of the shop is also famous.
t: I ate here in March 2023 ☺
Kakai Shokudo (along National Route 329)
Since it has the same name as the shop, and on top of that it's limited to 10 servings a day, I ordered the "Kakai Soba" 😁
Menu

Kakai soba　¥957

The soup has a strong pork bone base, and the noodles are a medium-thick straight type. The toppings are everything—pig's feet (tebichi), pork spare ribs (soki), braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), kelp, egg, and fish cake (kamaboko)—and it also comes with okara (soy pulp), for a very generous portion 😊

Rating (9/15): Solidly tasty. How about it when you're driving along the east coast of the northern region 😁　Also, I don't have a photo, but in front of the shop there's a vending machine selling "pig's feet (tebichi) (pig's trotters)" labeled "first in Japan." 城木屋.name: Shirokiya
城木屋.desc: A restaurant along National Route 449. Soki soba with a gently flavored broth, soft noodles, pork spare ribs (soki), and flavor-soaked knotted kelp. It has a wide menu beyond soba and becomes an izakaya at night. A pro baseball favorite, lined with autographs from Nippon-Ham players.

Shirokiya (along National Route 449)
In the "Nago Soba Map," "Shirokiya" is featured as shop 37 of 41
I ordered the "Soki Soba" that was introduced in the map.
Soki soba　¥650
Knotted kelp that has soaked up the flavor, tender pork spare ribs (soki), smooth soft noodles, and a gently flavored broth—delicious 😄

Rating (9/15): I think it's solidly tasty. There are lots of menu items besides soba, and at night they also run as an izakaya. It seems lots of pro baseball players come here too, with plenty of autographs and uniforms inside. During camp season, players from the Hokkaido Nippon-Ham Fighters might be dropping by ☺

Its distinctive feature is changing up the flavor with "Shimanero," an original habanero-based seasoning. A rare Okinawa soba shop that's also open in the evening.

After waiting a few minutes, the "Nankotsu Soba" came served in a black bowl with beautiful kintsugi, and it looks great too! 😋
Nankotsu soba (medium)　¥800
First, the soup. It's a light soup based on bonito broth, with a gentle flavor.
Nankotsu soba (medium)　¥800
